patterns.accessibility_notes: Keep headline and CTA in DOM text, preserve heading order, and keep tap targets at least 44px on touch devices.
patterns.performance_notes: Use static or CSS-driven visuals first; avoid blocking hero content behind canvas or video.

patterns.accessibility_notes: CTA copy must describe the action and outcome without relying on visual emphasis alone.
patterns.performance_notes: Keep the closing CTA lightweight and avoid blocking it behind animation or media.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Hero copy and CTA must remain DOM text with readable contrast, focus states, and equivalent static presentation for reduced motion.
patterns.performance_notes: Render text and CTA before motion; cap animation asset weight and avoid blocking LCP with canvas, video, or large script bundles.

risks: dot field competing with the offer
display word illegible at low dot counts
patterns.accessibility_notes: Read copy and CTA stay sharp DOM; dot-built display words carry a [data-dot-twin] DOM twin; the canvas is aria-hidden and the engine bails to a static frame under prefers-reduced-motion.
patterns.performance_notes: Procedural dots only — no stored frames. Cap the dot budget, start text before the canvas, and pause rendering when offscreen or hidden.
examples: dot-stage hero with a dot-built wordmark

risks: depth field competing with the offer
stored cloud reconstructing readable text in canvas
patterns.accessibility_notes: Read copy and CTA stay sharp DOM; the cloud canvas is aria-hidden and the engine freezes to a static home-pose frame under prefers-reduced-motion. The stored point cloud is gated by validatePointCloudScene (declared text needs a DOM twin; no primary content in canvas).
patterns.performance_notes: Bounded point budget (<=24000), procedural draw only, no per-frame allocation; pause and freeze offscreen or hidden. Inline the cloud only within budget; larger clouds fetch same-origin.
examples: 2.5D point-cloud brand backdrop with sharp DOM offer
depth-field hero over a faithful image cloud

patterns.accessibility_notes: Do not encode proof only in images; keep outcomes and labels as readable text.
patterns.performance_notes: Prefer compact media and lazy-load secondary proof visuals.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Ledger rows must be readable text with source/case references; use proof-led-section for broader narrative proof, not as a substitute for auditable items.
patterns.performance_notes: Prefer compact text-first entries and lazy-load optional case media.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Theme crossing must preserve readable text, heading order, contrast, focus states, and non-motion fallbacks.
patterns.performance_notes: Use static SVG/CSS first; add canvas/3D only after a performance budget and reduced-motion plan.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Do not duplicate hidden SEO text; make the real visible content accessible and indexable.
patterns.performance_notes: Keep visual assets decorative or supportive and lazy-load secondary media.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Mascot behavior must not be required to understand or operate the page.
patterns.performance_notes: Load model only on user intent or after idle; keep static HTML and CTA available first.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Link text must describe the demo target; do not rely on icon-only links.
patterns.performance_notes: Keep heavy demos outside the main marketing page and load them on demand.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Choice labels and CTA text must be readable DOM text with clear focus order and 44px touch targets.
patterns.performance_notes: Use CSS layout and text labels; avoid heavy interactive navigation before the offer path is understandable.

good_for: separating playful demos from core offer
requires: clear route back to main page
primary content and SEO text outside demo canvas
accessible text links for each demo
patterns.accessibility_notes: Each demo entry needs a text label and keyboard reachable link; the hub must remain navigable without canvas, pointer motion, or audio.
patterns.performance_notes: Load heavyweight demos on demand and keep a static summary or screenshot visible before any canvas or WebGL code runs.

patterns.accessibility_notes: The interaction must not be required to understand or activate content.
patterns.performance_notes: Use transform/opacity and throttle pointer work; no layout thrashing.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Respect prefers-reduced-motion and keep all content readable without scroll animation.
patterns.performance_notes: Avoid scroll event loops; prefer CSS timeline or intersection-driven class changes when available.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Keep case titles, outcomes, and CTA text in DOM order; horizontal layouts need keyboard and touch-safe access.
patterns.performance_notes: Use responsive layout and lazy-load secondary logos or thumbnails.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Use reveal only as enhancement; DOM order, visible text, focusable controls, and reduced-motion views must expose the same content.
patterns.performance_notes: Prefer CSS mask/clip-path/opacity transforms and avoid per-frame layout work; keep reveal effects optional on low-power devices.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Visual asymmetry must not change logical reading order.
patterns.performance_notes: Prefer CSS layout and real text over image-composited typography.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Product cards need readable names, prices, and actions in DOM text with 44px minimum touch targets.
patterns.performance_notes: Use responsive images, predictable card heights, and avoid loading all media at maximum resolution.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Variant controls need labels, selected states, disabled states, and error feedback that does not rely on color alone.
patterns.performance_notes: Prioritize product title, price, CTA, and main image before secondary media.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Drawer must trap focus while open, restore focus on close, and expose subtotal/quantity changes to assistive tech.
patterns.performance_notes: Keep the drawer lightweight and update totals deterministically from cart state, not from decorative UI state.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Steps need semantic headings, visible progress text, keyboard flow, and persistent validation messages.
patterns.performance_notes: Checkout should avoid heavy animation, 3D, video, and third-party scripts outside payment requirements.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Ratings must include text equivalents and review filters must be keyboard reachable.
patterns.performance_notes: Lazy-load long review lists below product decision content and reserve layout space.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Trust claims need concise text labels; icons alone are not enough.
patterns.performance_notes: Use simple inline icons or text, not large decorative media.

patterns.accessibility_notes: KPIs need text labels, units, deltas, and non-color status cues.
patterns.performance_notes: Render critical KPI text before secondary charts and avoid client-only metric hydration delays.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Filters need labels, visible selected values, keyboard flow, and a clear reset control.
patterns.performance_notes: Debounce expensive filters, preserve URL/state where useful, and show loading state for slow queries.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Tables need headers, keyboard reachable rows/actions, and readable responsive alternatives.
patterns.performance_notes: Use pagination or virtualization for large datasets and keep export logic tied to the active query.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Charts require textual summaries, source labels, and non-color encoding for critical states.
patterns.performance_notes: Avoid heavy chart bundles for simple visuals and lazy-load secondary chart detail.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Severity must be text-visible and new alerts should not steal focus unexpectedly.
patterns.performance_notes: Paginate or cap feed length and keep realtime updates optional for low-power devices.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Tables need semantic headers, focus states, keyboard row actions, and a mobile alternative when density is high.
patterns.performance_notes: Large lists need server-side pagination, stable sorting, and no full-dataset rendering by default.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Drawer must manage focus, announce record context, and warn before discarding unsaved changes.
patterns.performance_notes: Fetch heavy record detail on demand and cache cautiously with clear freshness rules.

patterns.accessibility_notes: State meaning must be readable as text and not rely on color alone.
patterns.performance_notes: Use simple DOM text and CSS tokens; avoid animated state chips in dense tables.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Selection counts, disabled reasons, confirmation text, and partial-failure results must be explicit.
patterns.performance_notes: Batch operations need bounded chunking, progress state, and recoverable partial-failure handling.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Saved views must expose the active state and not hide critical filter conditions.
patterns.performance_notes: Persist compact query state and validate role permissions when loading shared views.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Search and categories need semantic labels, keyboard flow, and no hover-only discovery.
patterns.performance_notes: Service links and labels must render as DOM text before enhancements.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Use real headings, short paragraphs, descriptive links, and readable line lengths.
patterns.performance_notes: Keep content server-rendered or static; do not hide primary instructions behind client-only widgets.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Every field needs labels, errors linked to inputs, keyboard flow, and a top error summary.
patterns.performance_notes: Avoid heavy step transitions and preserve form state during validation failures.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Severity and action must be text-visible; urgent notices should be announced without trapping focus.
patterns.performance_notes: Render notices cheaply and avoid layout shift by reserving stable space when persistent.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Contact links need descriptive text and address/office details must not be image-only.
patterns.performance_notes: Use simple text and links; maps are optional and should load after the core contact path.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Account state and next actions need visible headings, text labels, and predictable focus order.
patterns.performance_notes: Load primary account state first and lazy-load secondary activity lists.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Document rows need descriptive link text, file metadata, and keyboard reachable actions.
patterns.performance_notes: Do not preview large files by default; lazy-load previews and keep download actions explicit.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Messages need readable order, timestamps, focusable reply controls, and clear send/error states.
patterns.performance_notes: Paginate long threads and avoid loading all attachments eagerly.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Timeline order must match DOM order and status must be text-readable.
patterns.performance_notes: Use simple list layout on mobile and avoid scroll-jacked timeline effects.

patterns.accessibility_notes: Disabled or unavailable actions need accessible explanations and predictable focus handling.
patterns.performance_notes: Permission state should be fetched with account context and not guessed from client UI alone.

risks: text legibility over the stone photo
weak proof if only one image
patterns.accessibility_notes: Headline, CTA, heritage badge and photo caption are sharp DOM text on the stone; the only motion is a CSS light sweep that stops under prefers-reduced-motion (text shows sharp instantly).
patterns.performance_notes: CSS-only: a single looped light gradient on an isolated ::before layer + a one-shot text de-blur; no JS runtime, no stored frames.
examples: sandstone-wall hero with raking light for a mason
calm tactile-shadow opener for a craftsman
